headline: Roosters win a thriller NRL Grand Final 19-18, Microsoft has its best quarter since 1998, and the Middle East conflict deepens as Yemen's Saudi-backed government launches a major military campaign against Houthi forces.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft surged last night after news broke that the company added US$1 trillion in market value during its best quarter since 1998 — driven by its AI cloud business. Earnings are coming up and investors are piling in ahead of the results, betting the AI momentum keeps rolling.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE had a solid session today, lifted by broad strength in emerging market equities. The rising Aussie dollar (up 0.57% against the USD) also helps the international exposure in this fund feel more valuable in local terms.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara edged up slightly today — a modest positive move but nothing dramatic. Lithium sentiment remains subdued overall, and PLS continues to trade well below its purchase price. No major catalysts today.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google ticked up modestly last night. The stock has been under pressure because the market reckons Google's Gemini 4 AI model hasn't been the game-changer investors hoped for, and Q3 earnings are coming up. Cloud revenue hit $20B but there are questions about free cash flow. Cautious mood ahead of earnings.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI nudged up slightly today on the ASX, tracking general AI sector sentiment. No specific catalyst — the fund moves broadly with the fortunes of global AI-related stocks.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS ticked up today, reflecting last night's positive Wall Street session where the S&P 500 and NASDAQ both gained. Broad US market strength flowing through to the ASX-listed version of the fund.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG barely moved today — it's a diversified fund spread across global shares, so small moves are normal. No specific catalyst; it's simply tracking the overall market steadiness.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped a fraction last night — essentially flat. The stock remains in a wait-and-see mode as the market holds out for GTA VI news and clearer release timelines. Still sitting at a loss overall, but no new bad news today.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Riding a historic quarter — hold and watch earnings
watch_today.detail: Microsoft added US$1 trillion in market value last quarter — its best performance since 1998 — powered by AI cloud revenue. The stock jumped 1.29% last night. For a long-term holder this is exactly the kind of compounding you're investing for. Upcoming earnings are the next key moment to watch. No reason to sell; if anything, the long-term case looks stronger.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Q3 earnings approaching — Gemini AI disappointing so far
watch_today.detail: Google's Gemini 4 AI model has failed to excite the market the way Microsoft's AI story has, and questions about free cash flow are circulating ahead of Q3 earnings. The stock is still up 11% on your entry price. For a long-term holder, Google's fundamentals remain solid — Search, YouTube, and Cloud are all growing. Don't panic over a relative AI narrative lag; hold through earnings.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Still deep in the red — long-term patience required
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals is down nearly 45% on your purchase price. Today's tiny 0.54% gain doesn't change the picture. Lithium prices remain depressed globally. The long-term thesis — that lithium demand from EVs will eventually recover — is still intact, but this may take years to play out. There's no structural reason to sell here; the business is still operating. Sit tight, but be prepared for more volatility.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA VI is the whole story — stay patient
watch_today.detail: Take-Two was essentially flat last night. The stock is down ~13% on your cost. The entire investment case rests on GTA VI delivering blockbuster numbers when it eventually launches. There's no new bad news — just ongoing waiting. For a long-term holder this is a hold. Selling now would crystallise the loss before the catalyst arrives.

watch_today.title: Middle East escalation — oil worth watching this week
watch_today.detail: Crude oil fell below US$90 last night, but the situation is volatile: Yemen's Saudi-backed government launched a major new military campaign against Houthi forces, and Trump officials are reportedly discussing potential military action against Iran. Any escalation could spike oil prices fast, which would affect inflation and interest rates globally. Keep an eye on oil this week.

watch_today.title: Australian interest rates — closing in on world's highest
watch_today.detail: Australia is now close to having the highest interest rates in the developed world, according to SBS. Banks are also hiking fixed mortgage rates faster than the RBA is moving. This matters for anyone with a mortgage or thinking of buying property — and it affects the broader economy, which flows through to ASX earnings. The RBA's next move is a major watch item.

world.summary: The Middle East conflict continued to escalate today, with a new front opening in Yemen and US officials discussing potential military action against Iran. US midterm election tensions are also building, with both parties taking steps to secure the vote.

stories.title: Yemen's Saudi-backed government launches major military campaign against Houthi forces
stories.why_it_matters: Yemen's Saudi-backed government announced a major military campaign against the Houthi militia — an Iranian-backed armed group — deepening the already serious Middle East conflict. In response, the Houthis claimed to have targeted a refinery in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. This matters because Yemen has been a proxy battleground for Saudi Arabia and Iran for years, and any escalation risks disrupting oil supplies from the region, which affects petrol prices and inflation worldwide.

stories.title: Trump administration officials met at Camp David to discuss potential war with Iran
stories.why_it_matters: Senior Trump administration officials gathered at Camp David over the weekend to discuss the possibility of military action against Iran, according to CBS News. Separately, Iran told the US there is no military solution to the Middle East conflict. The discussions reflect how close the situation may be to direct US involvement — a potential game-changer for global oil markets, inflation, and broader geopolitical stability.

stories.title: Middle East oil exports surpass pre-war levels, but tanker attacks are increasing
stories.why_it_matters: Despite the ongoing war, Middle East oil exports actually topped pre-war levels for part of September — suggesting the region's production hasn't been hit as hard as feared. However, Houthi attacks on tankers in the Red Sea are increasing, which raises the risk of supply disruptions and higher shipping costs. More expensive shipping eventually feeds into higher prices for goods worldwide, including in Australia.

stories.title: Democrats and Republicans both scrambling ahead of US midterm elections
stories.why_it_matters: With US midterm elections approaching, Democrats are taking steps to secure Election Day from potential interference, while state officials are expressing frustration that the Trump administration isn't providing adequate support to protect the vote. The political stakes are high — the outcome of the midterms will determine control of Congress, which shapes US economic and foreign policy for the next two years. US political stability matters for global markets.

markets.summary: A broadly positive night on Wall Street last night — the S&P 500 and NASDAQ both gained, helped by Microsoft's stellar quarter. The ASX barely moved today, essentially flat. Oil slipped below US$90 amid Middle East uncertainty. The Aussie dollar rose to nearly 70 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Essentially flat today — not much to write home about on the local market.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Solid gain last night, helped by tech strength and Microsoft's historic quarter.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Tech-heavy index had a good night, with Microsoft and AI sentiment driving gains.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil dipped below $90 — despite Middle East tensions, supply fears haven't spiked prices yet. Worth watching.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold barely moved — holding near record highs as a safe haven amid global uncertainty.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar rose to nearly 70 US cents — good for Australians buying imports or travelling; slightly reduces the AUD value of US-dollar holdings.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is Australia's interest rates — we're now closing in on having the highest rates in the developed world. Banks are making it worse by hiking fixed rates faster than the RBA is moving.

stories.title: Australia closing in on world's highest interest rates
stories.why_it_matters: Australia now has interest rates that are among the highest in the developed world, with only one country ahead of us. This means Australian mortgage holders are paying more than almost anyone else globally. Higher rates slow down spending and economic growth, and they put pressure on property prices. If rates stay this high for longer, it could weigh on ASX earnings and household budgets across the country.

stories.title: Banks hiking fixed mortgage rates faster than the RBA
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's big banks are lifting their fixed-rate home loans faster than the Reserve Bank (RBA) is raising the official cash rate — meaning banks are pricing in future rate pain ahead of schedule. This is driven by rising funding costs for the banks themselves. For anyone on a fixed rate that's about to expire, the jump to a new rate could be a serious shock to the budget.

stories.title: Public frustration with the RBA grows — comedian calls for governor to quit
stories.why_it_matters: Public anger at the Reserve Bank is boiling over, with a well-known comedian publicly calling on the RBA governor to resign over the sustained interest rate pain Australians are experiencing. While it's a colourful story, it reflects a genuine undercurrent of community frustration — rates have been high for a prolonged period, and many Australians are feeling the squeeze on mortgages and cost of living.

ai.summary: The big AI story today is a historic moment: executives from OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and Meta all testified under oath before all 51 New York City Council members about the risks of AI. Meanwhile, Sam Altman argued the benefits of AI justify accepting some harm, and Trump appointed his top spy chief to run a new AI taskforce.

stories.title: OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and Meta executives testify under oath at NYC AI hearing
stories.why_it_matters: For the first time, the top executives from the four biggest AI companies — OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and Meta — testified under oath before all 51 members of the New York City Council on the risks their technology poses. This is significant because it signals that AI regulation is moving from abstract debates into real government accountability. City and state governments are increasingly stepping in as federal regulation has lagged. Expect more hearings and potentially laws that could affect how these companies operate.

stories.title: Sam Altman says AI benefits justify accepting some harm
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, speaking at the NYC hearing, made a blunt argument: the enormous benefits AI will deliver to society — in medicine, science, productivity — are worth accepting some degree of risk and potential harm along the way. This is a significant public stance, essentially arguing against heavy-handed restrictions. Critics will push back that it's the companies themselves deciding what 'acceptable harm' looks like, which is exactly why these hearings are being held.

stories.title: Trump appoints top intelligence chief to lead new AI taskforce
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has appointed its director of national intelligence — the government's top spy boss — to lead a new AI taskforce. This signals the administration views AI primarily through a national security lens, rather than an economic or consumer-protection one. Expect the taskforce to focus on military AI, surveillance technology, and preventing rivals like China from gaining an AI advantage — rather than, say, protecting everyday users from chatbot harms.

stories.title: Where is Google's Gemini 3.5 Pro? The missing AI model raising questions
stories.why_it_matters: Google had been expected to release Gemini 3.5 Pro — an upgraded version of its flagship AI model — but it seems to have quietly disappeared from Google's roadmap. Mashable is asking where it went. This matters because it feeds into the narrative that Google is struggling to keep pace with OpenAI and Anthropic in releasing competitive AI models, which is weighing on GOOGL stock and investor confidence in the company's AI strategy.

sport.summary: The Roosters won a heart-stopping NRL Grand Final 19-18 over the Knights last night. AFL trade period is under way with plenty of movement expected across the league.

stories.title: Sydney Roosters win NRL Grand Final 19-18 over Newcastle Knights
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters held off a brave Newcastle Knights outfit 19-18 in a nail-biting NRL Grand Final at Accor Stadium last Sunday night. The Roosters' billionaire owner is already teasing big signings after the club's second grand final win in recent years. There's also debate about a star player — reportedly on $850k — whose 'massive impact' grand final performance may have been his last for the club. The Knights pushed them all the way in what The Guardian called a 'thrilling' contest.

stories.title: Tigers recruit humiliates Panthers 54 points in State Championship
stories.why_it_matters: A new Tigers recruit put on a show in the State Championship, embarrassing the Panthers in a 54-point blowout. Fox Sports reports it as one of the stand-out individual performances of the representative season — a serious statement from the Tigers heading into next year.

stories.title: AFL trade period kicks off — what every club needs
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL trade period has officially opened, and Fox Sports has published a comprehensive 18-club guide on what each team needs. Port Adelaide's list manager is calling for a major rule change to how the trade period works. Meanwhile, the AFL Draft Combine was held over the weekend, with key results and standout performers emerging from the testing. If your club is in the market, now is the time to watch closely.

stories.title: Koori Knockout Finals Day — full results
stories.why_it_matters: Finals day at the Koori Knockout was held on the weekend, one of the most culturally significant community footy events in the country. Full results are in — the Telegraph has the complete wrap from an important day for First Nations rugby league communities across NSW.
